dialogue.text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent, and I'll be conducting your examination today. Could you tell me what you were doing right before the episode of loss of consciousness occurred?
I had just finished using the bathroom - you know, urinating - and then the next thing I knew, I was waking up on the floor with my wife standing over me looking terrified.
Were you experiencing any lightheadedness, dizziness, or chest discomfort right before you passed out?
No, not really - I felt completely fine before it happened. Maybe just a little bit lightheaded for a split second right as I finished, but nothing that made me think I was going to pass out.
Did you notice any unusual heart racing or palpitations right before losing consciousness, and did anyone witness any abnormal body movements or shaking while you were out?

No, I didn't feel my heart racing or anything like that beforehand. And my wife said I just sort of collapsed - she didn't see any shaking or jerking movements, I was just lying there still until I woke up.
Were you able to control your bladder completely, or did you experience any incontinence during the episode?
No, I didn't have any accidents or anything like that - everything was completely normal in that regard. My wife didn't notice anything either when she found me.
Did you bite your tongue or experience any confusion after regaining consciousness?
No, I didn't bite my tongue, and honestly I felt pretty clear-headed as soon as I woke up. I knew exactly where I was and what had happened - no confusion at all.
REQUEST TEST: Electrocardiogram (ECG)
RESULTS: Electrocardiogram (ECG) - No abnormalities detected. Normal sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, normal intervals (PR, QRS, QT), no ST-segment changes, no arrhythmias noted.
"Thank you. Did you experience any unusual sweating, nausea, or tunnel vision in the moments leading up to the episode?"
No, nothing like that - no sweating, no nausea, no vision changes. Like I said, I felt totally normal right up until that brief moment of lightheadedness, and then I was out.
REQUEST TEST: Orthostatic_Vital_Signs

RESULTS: Orthostatic Vital Signs - Normal readings. No significant orthostatic changes detected. Blood pressure and heart rate remain stable when changing from lying to standing position, with no evidence of orthostatic hypotension.
REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC) - All parameters within normal limits. Hemoglobin, hematocrit, white blood cell count, and platelet count are all normal. No evidence of anemia or infection.
Did you experience any headache, weakness on one side of your body, or difficulty speaking after you woke up?
No, nothing like that at all. When I woke up, I felt completely normal - no headache, no weakness anywhere, and I could speak just fine right away.
Did you feel any sudden shortness of breath, chest pressure, or pain in your chest or arm right before or after the event?
No, no chest pain or pressure at all, and my breathing was fine. I didn't have any pain in my arms or anywhere else either - really, the whole thing just happened out of nowhere.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Vasovagal syncope
